comparator.sourceNotes: The corrected Chemistry pathway closes 60+60+60 with 82.5 EC compulsory study, 52.5 EC restricted choice and 45 EC genuine profiling. Biochemical Methods/Academic Formation 2 is compulsory; Inorganic/Solid-State Chemistry is selected, not universal. The bounded set includes the required Category 2 choice and satisfies the stronger formal level minima. Extra chemistry examples are not used to erase genuine profiling. The dated 2025-entry page is context only. Formal and current required/advanced-course evidence support Dutch plus English.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names neither official study path. Moleculen en Materialen is listed before Moleculen en Leven on the current curriculum page, so it is selected neutrally before UCR fit is considered. The concrete pathway uses a coherent set of published materials, physical, inorganic, analytical and supporting-methods courses while satisfying the displayed category structure.

core: Biomolecules, proteins, cells, biochemistry and molecular laboratory investigation
Materials behaviour, sustainable chemistry, lifecycle impacts, environmental biogeochemistry, energy and resource recovery
Experimental, laboratory, data and research methods for molecular, material and environmental questions
adjacent: Molecular disease mechanisms, medicines and therapeutic research
Mathematics, programming, data analysis and computational modelling for molecular and material systems

trace: develops a product concept, fabrication method and prototype and evaluates sustainability and cost; it supports chemical-product design questions without teaching chemical synthesis or process equipment
develops data cleaning, visualisation and analysis for experimental, environmental and materials data
supplies structured programming, testing and debugging for quantitative analysis and system models
introduces calculus, matrices, complex numbers and differential equations used in quantitative process and environmental models
teaches stable numerical solution methods for equations, interpolation, integration and differential equations
develops probability, distributions, estimation and simulation for experimental and model uncertainty
examines recycling, recovery and remediation technologies, resource security, inorganic chemistry and laboratory work for circular material systems
examines how public and private actors make and implement sustainability policy, a concrete institutional dimension of lower-impact industrial transition
uses field and laboratory analyses to study soil properties, remediation and aquifers as material and environmental systems
uses system modelling, proxies and isotope tracers to analyse linked Earth-system processes and greenhouse-gas pathways
studies aqueous and mineral biogeochemical processes, water treatment and resource recovery using geochemical modelling
conducts advanced research on resources, geothermal energy, carbon capture and waste storage
establishes physics, chemistry, materials, mathematics and modelling foundations for sustainability problems
extends the sustainability foundation through waves, chemistry and materials science in an applied project
examines climate drivers, impacts, mitigation, renewable energy and carbon storage as the context for lower-impact production
directly evaluates environmental impacts of products and processes across their lifecycle and develops circular-economy planning
assesses energy-use patterns and technically and economically evaluates solar, wind and bioenergy system designs
provides team-based applied research with an external organisation on a sustainability problem
introduces biochemistry, macromolecules, cells and DNA as a biological foundation for molecular and biotechnology questions
studies eukaryotic and prokaryotic cell biology and current life-science research methods
directly studies proteins, sugars, lipids, nucleic acids, metabolic pathways and biotechnology applications
provides biochemical and molecular laboratory work with proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics
studies molecular genetics, cell injury, inflammation, repair and disease as one health-facing application of molecular science
implements regression, classification, resampling and clustering for prediction and pattern discovery in molecular-life and biomedical data
develops matrix, vector and eigenvalue methods for multivariable biological and pharmacological models
studies disease frequency, risk, screening and causal evidence, supporting population-level assessment of therapeutic effectiveness and safety
connects anatomical structure with organ-system function and medical imaging, locating therapeutic action and disease effects within the human body
directly studies drug targets, molecular interactions, pharmacokinetics, toxicity and quantitative concentration-response relationships
studies immune recognition, host-pathogen interactions and immunopathology as disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets
derives pathophysiology across organ systems from anatomy and physiology, providing the disease-mechanism basis for rational intervention
studies neurobiology, disorders, animal models, laboratory techniques and research ethics as one concrete biomedical application domain
studies neural mechanisms of perception and action, supplying organ-system function relevant to neuroactive drug effects without claiming neuropharmacology
introduces brain and behavioural science plus experimental methods as the formal foundation for later treatment-evidence synthesis and neural applications
studies homeostasis, signalling and integrated organ-system physiology needed to understand drug effects in the human body
develops regression, multivariate analysis and experimental inference for biomedical and treatment-response evidence
performs systematic review and meta-analysis in R to estimate treatment effects and assess consistency across studies

alternatives.label: Biochemistry, materials & sustainable resource systems
alternatives.concept: Combine biomolecular and laboratory science with environmental biogeochemistry, materials and resource recovery, lifecycle analysis, renewable systems, mathematics, programming and data methods. This is a related response to molecular, materials and sustainable-chemistry interests, not full Chemistry equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines biochemistry and molecular laboratory work with materials, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery, lifecycle analysis, renewable systems and quantitative methods; the label does not claim organic, inorganic, analytical or physical chemistry depth.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Life/health foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, laboratory work and molecular pathology; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and every dependent advanced environmental/resource course; Mathematical Methods precedes numerical methods and probability/statistics.

alternatives.label: Molecular life science, disease & therapeutic research
alternatives.concept: Study proteins, cells and biomolecular function through biochemistry, molecular and cellular biology, physiology, pharmacology, pathology, immunology, laboratory research, epidemiology and quantitative methods. Preserve the absence of a cumulative chemistry, synthesis and spectroscopy sequence explicitly.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by biomolecules, molecular/physiological biology, disease mechanisms, pharmacology and biomedical research; the label describes molecular life science rather than chemistry as a discipline.
progression: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and six level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Life/health foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory work and all advanced biomedical courses; biochemistry and physiology precede Pharmacology. Brain-and-behaviour foundations precede Perception & Action and the Advanced Research Seminar. Mathematical Methods precedes numerical methods, linear algebra and probability/statistics, while introductory data analysis precedes machine learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Thirteen courses / 97.5 EC differ in each direction. Environmental biogeochemistry, materials, lifecycle, resource-recovery, renewable-system and sustainability courses are replaced by physiology, anatomy, pharmacology, immunology, epidemiology, biomedical statistics and disease study. The choice therefore shifts from sustainable materials and resource systems to molecular life, disease and therapeutic research.

candidates.label: Molecules and life, disease and therapeutic research
Specialist molecular, reaction, analytical and laboratory chemistry

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. A third specialist chemistry route is not defensible because the workbook lacks cumulative general, organic, inorganic, analytical, physical and quantum chemistry; synthesis, spectroscopy and structure determination; reaction mechanisms, electrochemistry and solid-state chemistry; and a chemistry laboratory progression. The included routes preserve those gaps rather than relabelling biochemistry, sustainability or quantitative courses as full chemistry.

blocks: Biomolecules, cells, disease and therapeutic research
Both study biomolecular and cellular processes; UCR provides molecular cell biology rather than the comparator’s advanced chemistry framing.
Both directly study proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, nucleic acids and metabolism; UCR does not replace the surrounding chemistry sequence.
Both develop biochemical experimental methods; UCR supplies a life-science laboratory rather than analytical or synthetic chemistry training.
Both establish mathematical foundations for scientific study; UCR is a general mathematical-methods course rather than mathematics and physics taught within chemistry.
Both extend quantitative scientific foundations; UCR contributes linear algebra but not the comparator’s chemistry-specific physics content.
Both develop computational mathematical methods; UCR teaches numerical methods but not molecular modelling as a chemistry specialism.
Both develop scientific data analysis; UCR does not supply the comparator’s spectroscopy component.
Materials, environmental chemistry, energy and resources
Both address materials and inorganic concepts; UCR provides introductory sustainability-oriented chemistry and materials science rather than a dedicated inorganic and solid-state chemistry course.
Specialist chemistry, thesis and open profile
UCR has no organic-chemistry and spectroscopy sequence.
UCR has no dedicated physical and inorganic chemistry course.
UCR has no quantum and inorganic chemistry sequence.
UCR has no analytical chemistry course or analytical-chemistry laboratory progression.
UCR has no second physical chemistry course.
The genuine 22.5-EC profiling space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.
UCR has no X-ray and electron structure-determination course.
UCR has no advanced physical chemistry sequence.
UCR sustainability and Earth-science materials content does not replace dedicated chemistry of solids and surfaces.
The compulsory Chemistry thesis remains separate; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and not scheduled degree credit.
The second genuine 22.5-EC profiling component remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine biochemistry and molecular laboratory work with either sustainable materials/resource systems or molecular life, disease and therapeutic research. UCR does not reproduce the comparator’s cumulative organic, inorganic, analytical, physical and quantum chemistry; synthesis, spectroscopy, structure determination, electrochemistry and solid-state chemistry; or chemistry-specific laboratory and thesis progression.
